judged_text: When the parsed response lacks refresh_token (always true for the sync endpoint, whose documented response contains only access_token and expiry), the function mutates data to `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`, and callers (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts ~98-101, office365calendar CalendarService.ts ~263-270) then persist this merged/stripped object over the credential key via prisma.credential.update. Sync-mode refreshes overwrite the stored credential with a placeholder refresh_token and drop expiry_date and other real fields; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ever removed or the sync endpoint is down, previously-working Google and Outlook credentials are permanently broken (no valid refresh_token to fall back to).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when sync-mode is enabled it accepts responses without `refresh_token` and then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result is merged into the existing credential via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, which will overwrite a previously valid `refresh_token` with the placeholder when the sync endpoint returns only `access_token`/expiry. That can permanently corrupt stored credentials and break future non-sync refreshes. (The finding’s mention of Google Calendar specifically overwriting due to the placeholder is less directly supported because Google passes `googleCredentials`—which already contains a refresh_token—into `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, but the Office365 overwrite scenario is clearly shown.)
